author: cli
text: Re-read 2026-08-17. Every claim checked against the body. The last-segment index exists and is used: _suffix_index is a defaultdict keyed by q.rsplit('.',1)[-1], rebuilt only when by_qualname changes size, so a suffix lookup is a dict hit rather than a scan - the O(1) vs O(entities) claim is real. Hybrid refs (file.py:name and path/file.py:name) are still handled, and tiered matching still prefers an exact last component before falling back. NOTE FOR 0.56.0: this function is where the one-name-one-producer work lands, because bare names arriving here cannot currently match entities registered with a /arity or #N disambiguator. Expect this confirm to stale then, correctly.

author: cli
text: Re-confirmed at 0.56.0. Every earlier claim still holds - hybrid refs, tiered matching, the last-segment index and its performance argument. The note above records what this release changed.

author: agent
text:
Re-read at 0.57.1, claim by claim. The suffix index, its O(1) argument, refs.short_of keying both sides, arity breaking an overload tie only when the reference declares one, and the production-over-test fallback all still hold - they MOVED into candidates() unchanged rather than being altered.

Comment rot answered, not confirmed away: the block describing the base-name index was left behind in resolve() when its code moved, so the file carried it twice and the copy in resolve() described code that was no longer there. Deleted; the docstring now names candidates() as its home and states the two reasons resolve() returns None, which is the thing a reader of this function most needs and the thing it did not say.
